content.title: Graphic Reset Relay | Identity Cards Alternate with Action Proofs
content.summary: Begin with one compact identity activation, then alternate a stable graphic reset with short physical capability proofs. Raise the later action demand and carry the peak motion contour into a held complete-subject lockup.

quick_start.input_format: The same original character or machine + fixed graphic identity card + at least 2 different action certificates + graphic reset separation + subsequent ability upgrade + action outline recovery to final full body lock
quick_start.recommended_input: An original folding orbital rescue drone first completes its identity activation with white ceramic armor, copper-colored joints and a single red icon; the graphite gray technology card resets its identity, and then proves its two abilities by grabbing floating equipment and lifting the external shield; finally, the oblique outlines of the drone and the shield are retracted into the final full-body technology card.
required_anchors: Begin with one compact identity activation before showing the complete subject.
Establish one clearly different graphic reset mode that preserves subject silhouette and proportions.
Raise physical demand in the later action proof while keeping the same defining silhouette and direction cues.
Carry the peak action contour into the final graphic state and hold a complete-subject lockup.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Begin with one compact identity activation, then alternate a stable graphic reset with short physical capability proofs. Raise the later action demand and carry the peak motion contour into a held complete-subject lockup.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Open on one compact identity activation, then alternate a stable graphic reset mode with short physical proof scenes. Each reset must re-establish the same subject through recurring silhouette, proportion or layout anchors, and each action block must answer one new capability question without changing identity. Reserve the last reset to absorb the peak action contour and resolve it into a held complete-subject lockup.

invariants.rule: Begin with one compact identity activation before showing the complete subject.
invariants.purpose: Creates a recognition cue that later resets can verify.
invariants.ablation_failure: Opening on the finished full-body card removes the identity question and weakens later confirmation.

invariants.rule: Establish one clearly different graphic reset mode that preserves subject silhouette and proportions.
invariants.purpose: Provides a stable comparison baseline between moving proof scenes.
invariants.ablation_failure: If the reset redesigns the subject or uses unrelated layouts, the sequence becomes a generic montage.

invariants.rule: Alternate reset and action so every action block proves one distinct capability while the next reset restores identity legibility.
invariants.purpose: Lets physical escalation accumulate without hiding subject drift.
invariants.ablation_failure: Uninterrupted action loses the verification rhythm; uninterrupted cards provide no capability proof.

invariants.rule: Raise physical demand in the later action proof while keeping the same defining silhouette and direction cues.
invariants.purpose: Creates escalation that remains auditable against the prior reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: A weaker or unrelated second action feels like repetition rather than progression.

invariants.rule: Carry the peak action contour into the final graphic state and hold a complete-subject lockup.
invariants.purpose: Converts motion into a readable terminal identity result.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on motion blur, an isolated word or a cropped body denies final verification.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source brown-haired bespectacled young male character in a grey sleeveless hoodie and fingerless gloves
the source green glowing spectacle activation and fingertip-to-lens gesture
the source white rooftop or salt-flat action space with distant mountains and dark opponent
the source black, white, cyan and neon-yellow oversized editorial card system
the source circular brush rings, exact action choreography and final crouched pose
the source visible words RunningHUB, HERO and YOU

instantiations.concept: An original folding orbital rescue drone begins with one amber beacon iris activating in macro. A copper technical card locks its triangular silhouette, then a hangar test proves one magnetic grapple action. The card resets with the same dimensions before an exterior debris-lift proof; the lifted diagonal contour becomes a final slate-blue specification lockup showing the complete drone and secured cargo.

instantiations.concept: In tactile stop-motion, an original seed-sorting automaton starts when one ceramic eye shutter opens. A physical pegboard card records its squat outline, followed by one paper-seed pickup test. The pegboard resets before a steeper felt-ramp delivery; the ramp pose transfers into a final shadow-box catalog display that holds the complete machine and delivered seed tray.
